The Staff

Meet the Coaches

Coach Twillie III

Head Coach • Organization

Credentials: USA Basketball Gold Licensed Coach • Licensed AAU Member • National Association of Basketball Coaches (NABC) Member

With a decade of coaching experience and a lifetime of athletic dedication, Coach Twillie brings a wealth of knowledge, passion, and elite training standards to our program. A versatile athlete from the start, Coach Twillie competed in basketball, track, and soccer during his school years, developing a deep understanding of multi-sport athleticism, speed mechanics, and competitive drive. This diverse sports background heavily influences his holistic approach to player development today.

Coaching Journey
Coach Twillie has spent the last 10 years mentoring young athletes and building successful programs across multiple competitive tiers:

Founder & Head Coach, Young Shooterz Basketball (2022–Present): Launched the program to provide elite skill development, basketball IQ training, and mentorship for local youth.

Head Coach, YMCA Youth Leagues (2018–2021): Focused on building foundational skills, teamwork, and a love for the game in a high-energy community environment.

Assistant Coach, Harmony School (2017): Contributed to strategic game planning and varsity-level player development.

Coaching Philosophy
“My goal is to develop fundamentally sound, high-IQ basketball players while instilling the discipline, accountability, and work ethic required to succeed both on and off the court.”

By holding elite-level certifications from USA Basketball (Gold License) and the NABC, Coach Twillie ensures that our athletes are learning under the highest standard of safety, modern skill-development techniques, and ethical coaching practices certified at the national level.

Coach Hawthorne

Head Coach • 9th Grade Boys

I am Anthony Allen Hawthorne, and I have been in love with the game of basketball since I was an 8-year-old kid first picking up a ball. I played varsity basketball as a sophomore in high school and started all of my last three years. I was heavily recruited by Oklahoma and LSU, but I wanted to develop more, so I decided to play college ball at a junior college for two years. I ended up playing one year before a coaching scandal hit my freshman year. When that happened, I lost track of things and started out training kids after college. I always said that if I did not go pro, I would want to give back to the game of basketball by coaching, training, and mentoring kids on the come-up! I started training in 2012 and started coaching my own AAU team shortly after, around 2014. In August 2022, I started coaching at a private high school in Dallas by the name of The Winston High School. I am the middle school boys head coach and the varsity boys assistant coach. This school had never made the playoffs in its history before I came, and now we have been to the playoffs every year, including the Elite 8 in my second year there. I am beyond proud of all the work I have put in and the lives I’ve touched over time. In 2023–2024, I received a Coach of the Year award! I am currently still there as an assistant coach while I look to further my career in a head position somewhere, when God says it’s my turn! My passion for the game of basketball is unmatched in my opinion, and I truly enjoy coaching the younger generation!

Coach Ray

Assistant Coach • HS Girls

Hello, my name is Coach Ray. I am a lifelong competitor who has developed an elite basketball IQ through years of AAU competition and extensive film study. My basketball journey took me from Shawnee Heights High School to the collegiate level at Johnson County Community College, where I played shooting guard. Known for my dynamic shooting, ball-handling ability, and high-level understanding of the game, I pride myself on reading defenses, anticipating plays, and creating high-percentage scoring opportunities for my team. On the defensive end, I built a reputation as a relentless perimeter defender, earning MVP awards throughout my career, along with multiple All-Team and All-Tournament honors. My accomplishments also include being named the 2011 USSSA Mo-Kan Midwest Free Throw Champion and helping lead my team to both the Jayhawk East Conference Championship and NJCAA Region VI Championship in 2017. Through discipline, leadership, and a commitment to excellence on both ends of the floor, I established myself as a true two-way player and leader. I’ve been with Young Shooterz for the past nine months, and it has been a blessing to be part of such an amazing coaching staff. I’m excited to see what the Lord has in store for our team this season and seasons to come! I am committed to continuing my growth as both a coach and mentor.

Coach Watts

Head Coach • 7th Boys Red

Coach Watts' basketball background started from playing youth leagues through his senior year of varsity. He began his coaching journey with the Young Shooterz organization and spent three years as a high school girls' assistant coach. As a head coach, Watts has successfully led developmental 5th-grade girls and 7th-grade boys, focusing on player growth and lifelong athletic fundamentals.

The Mission

About the Program

About the Young Shooterz Program

As a 501(c)(3) Nonprofit Christian basketball organization, our heart is to mentor athletes through the game they love while building a strong spiritual foundation. To reach more youth and expand our impact, we need like-minded leaders, partners, and supporters who want to pour into our mission.

You can be an intricate part of this exciting new chapter. Want to make a lasting impact? Email youngshooterz2021@gmail.com and learn how you can get involved in our expansion process.
